root_cause.text: The `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()` function did not check the return status or firmware error code from `__sev_do_cmd_locked()` before copying the ID blob to userspace, so a failed PSP command (e.g., due to an invalid length) could cause a copy of data beyond the kernel-allocated buffer, leading to a slab-out-of-bounds read and information leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;` before the `copy_to_user()` call, preventing the copy when the firmware command fails. The CVE description explicitly states: "don't attempt to copy the ID blob to userspace if the firmware command failed. If the failure was due to an invalid length ... copying the number of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace." The KASAN report confirms the out-of-bounds access occurs in `copy_to_user` within `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2`.

intent_record.what: Added a conditional check after a function call (sev_do_get_id2) that jumps to the e_free label if the return value ret is non-zero or if argp->error is set (with a WARN_ON_ONCE).
intent_record.how: This change prevents the function from proceeding to copy_to_user or other operations when an error has occurred, ensuring that errors are properly handled and resources are freed early.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code in sev_ioctl_do_get_id2() does not check the return value of __sev_do_cmd_locked() before using data.len to copy back to userspace. If the PSP command fails, data.len may be stale (e.g., the user-provided length) and the copy_to_user with that length can read beyond the allocated id_blob buffer, causing a slab-out-of-bounds read and information leak. Specifically, after 'ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_GET_ID, &data, &argp->error);' the code sets 'input.length = data.len;' and later does 'if (copy_to_user(input_address, id_blob, data.len))' without any error check on ret, so a failed command still copies data based on an uncontrolled length.
